name: Bedwyr

attributes.attribute: Welsh hero in the tale Kuluhch and Olwen
reduced to Arthur's butler in later Arthurian literature
cast the sword Excalibur into the water

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Bedwyr is a Welsh hero. His other names are Bedivere and Bedwyr fab Bedrawg. He appears in the Welsh tale of Kulhwch and Olwen, where he is a warrior of high standing. He is brave and never shies from a fight. He is handsome, though less so than the hero Arthur and far less than Lancelot. In later Arthurian stories his standing falls. Writers call him only Arthur's butler. Yet one remnant of his old importance survives. Bedwyr must throw the great sword Excalibur into the water. The Lady of the Lake then reclaims it. After that task, Bedwyr places the dying king in the boat that heads to Avalon.

okr.objective: Bedwyr is a Welsh hero whose standing drops to that of Arthur's butler even as he stays trusted with Excalibur.
